lessons.title: Introduction and Why It Matters
lessons.body: Cyanidation is a chemical process used to extract gold from low-grade ore. It involves dissolving gold in a sodium cyanide solution, then recovering it. This method is dangerous because cyanide is highly toxic. In Africa, many small-scale miners use cyanidation without proper safety, leading to poisonings and environmental damage. For example, in Tanzania and Ghana, illegal cyanide use has contaminated rivers. But cyanidation is also important: it allows recovery of fine gold that panning or sluicing misses. In this module, you will learn the correct and safe way to do cyanidation, if you must. But remember: cyanide can kill you in minutes. Never work alone. Always have a safety plan. This method is not for beginners. If you can use gravity separation or mercury-free methods, do that instead. But if you have no choice, learn the right way. We will cover tools, step-by-step method, common mistakes, safety, and a practical exercise. This is dangerous work, but with knowledge, you can reduce the risk. Always prioritize life over gold.

lessons.title: Tools and Materials
lessons.body: To do cyanidation, you need specific tools and chemicals. First, sodium cyanide (NaCN) or potassium cyanide (KCN) in powder or briquette form. Buy from a licensed supplier; never buy from informal markets. You need a leaching tank: a plastic or stainless steel drum, at least 200 liters, with a lid. Do not use galvanized metal because cyanide reacts with zinc. You need a pH meter or pH paper to keep pH above 10.5. Lime (calcium hydroxide) to raise pH. You need a respirator with cyanide filters, chemical goggles, rubber gloves, and a rubber apron. Always have a buddy. For aeration, you need an air pump or a stirrer. For recovery, you need zinc dust or activated carbon. For testing, you need a gold pan and a scale. For safety, have a first aid kit and a cyanide antidote kit (amyl nitrite, sodium nitrite, sodium thiosulfate). Store chemicals in a locked, ventilated area away from acids. Never store cyanide near acids because it releases deadly hydrogen cyanide gas. Keep a bucket of bleach and water to neutralize spills. Work outdoors or in a well-ventilated shed. Never work in a closed room. Have a hose with water for washing. All these tools are available in most African cities, but they cost money. Do not improvise with dangerous substitutes.

lessons.title: Step by Step Method
lessons.body: First, crush your ore to fine powder, like sand. You can use a ball mill or stamp mill. The finer the ore, the better the gold recovery. Next, mix water and ore in the leaching tank. Use 1 part ore to 3 parts water. Add lime to raise pH to 10.5-11.0. Test with pH paper. Then add sodium cyanide. A typical dose is 0.5 to 2 grams of cyanide per liter of water. For a 200-liter tank, start with 100 grams of cyanide. Stir gently for 24 to 48 hours. Keep the tank covered to prevent animals or people from drinking. After leaching, let solids settle. Siphon off the clear liquid (pregnant solution) into another tank. Now recover gold. Two methods: zinc precipitation or carbon adsorption. For zinc, add zinc dust to the solution. Gold precipitates as a black mud. For carbon, add activated carbon; gold attaches to carbon. Then burn the carbon or treat with caustic soda to recover gold. Finally, smelt the gold mud with borax and soda ash in a furnace. Always test the tailings to see if gold remains. If yes, repeat leaching. Never pour waste into rivers. Neutralize waste with bleach or hydrogen peroxide before disposal. Work in a well-ventilated area. Always wear full protective gear. Never eat, drink, or smoke during the process.

lessons.title: Common Mistakes and Fixes
lessons.body: Mistake 1: Using too much cyanide. This wastes money and increases danger. Fix: Use the correct dose, 0.5-2 g/L. Test with a cyanide test kit. Mistake 2: Not controlling pH. If pH drops below 10, hydrogen cyanide gas forms. Fix: Add lime regularly and check pH every hour. Mistake 3: Leaching for too short a time. Gold may not fully dissolve. Fix: Leach for at least 24 hours, preferably 48. Mistake 4: Using dirty water or acid-contaminated water. This consumes cyanide. Fix: Use clean water, and never mix with acid. Mistake 5: Not wearing protective gear. Cyanide can be absorbed through skin. Fix: Always wear gloves, goggles, and respirator. Mistake 6: Storing cyanide near acids. This creates deadly gas. Fix: Store separately in locked cabinets. Mistake 7: Pouring waste into the environment. This kills fish and people. Fix: Neutralize with bleach (1 part bleach to 10 parts waste) and test before disposal. Mistake 8: Working alone. If you collapse, no one helps. Fix: Always have a buddy who knows first aid. Mistake 9: Using metal containers that react with cyanide. Fix: Use plastic or stainless steel. Mistake 10: Not having an antidote kit. Fix: Keep amyl nitrite and sodium thiosulfate on site. Learn to use them. These mistakes are common in African small-scale mining. Avoid them to stay alive.

lessons.title: Safety and Best Practice
lessons.body: Cyanide is a fast-acting poison. It stops your cells from using oxygen. You can die within minutes. Safety is not optional. First, never work alone. Always have a trained buddy. Second, wear full protective equipment: respirator with cyanide cartridges, chemical goggles, rubber gloves, rubber apron, and rubber boots. Third, work in a well-ventilated area, preferably outdoors. Never work in a closed room. Fourth, have a safety plan. Know where the nearest clinic is and how to get there. Keep a cyanide antidote kit on site. Amyl nitrite ampoules, sodium nitrite, and sodium thiosulfate. Learn how to use them. Fifth, never eat, drink, or smoke while working. Wash hands thoroughly after work. Sixth, store cyanide in a locked, dry, ventilated area away from acids. Seventh, have a spill kit: bleach, water, and sand. If a spill happens, evacuate, ventilate, and neutralize with bleach. Eighth, test the air for hydrogen cyanide gas using a gas detector. If you smell bitter almonds, that is dangerous; but not everyone can smell it. Ninth, train everyone on the dangers. Tenth, keep records of chemical use. In Africa, many miners die because they ignore safety. Do not be one of them. If you feel dizzy, headache, or short of breath, get fresh air immediately and seek help. Always prioritize life over gold.

lessons.title: Practical Exercise
lessons.body: In this exercise, you will leach a small sample of gold ore using cyanide, under supervision. You will need: 1 kg of crushed ore, 3 liters of water, 5 grams of sodium cyanide, 10 grams of lime, a 10-liter plastic bucket, a stirrer, pH paper, gloves, goggles, respirator, and a buddy. First, put on all protective gear. Work outdoors. Mix water and ore in the bucket. Add lime until pH is 10.5-11.0. Then add cyanide slowly while stirring. Cover the bucket and stir every hour for 24 hours. After 24 hours, let solids settle. Carefully pour off the clear liquid into another bucket. Add 1 gram of zinc dust to the liquid. Stir for 30 minutes. A grey or black precipitate will form. Let it settle, then pour off the liquid. The precipitate is your gold concentrate. Dry it and smelt with borax. Weigh the gold. Calculate recovery: (gold recovered / gold in ore) x 100. For example, if ore had 0.1 grams and you recovered 0.08 grams, recovery is 80%. If recovery is low, check pH, cyanide dose, and leaching time. After the exercise, neutralize all waste with bleach (1 part bleach to 10 parts waste). Test with pH paper and cyanide test strips before disposal. Clean all tools with soap and water. Wash your hands and face. Report any spills or symptoms immediately. This exercise teaches you the process but remember: cyanide is deadly. Never do this without proper training and safety equipment.

quiz.q: What is the main danger of cyanidation?
options: D) It produces too much gold
quiz.explanation: Cyanide can kill quickly by stopping oxygen use in cells.

quiz.q: Why is cyanidation used in gold mining?
options: B) It recovers fine gold from low-grade ore
quiz.explanation: Cyanidation dissolves fine gold that other methods miss.

quiz.q: Which chemical is used to raise pH in cyanidation?
quiz.explanation: Lime (calcium hydroxide) raises pH to safe levels above 10.5.

quiz.q: What is the recommended pH range for cyanidation?
quiz.explanation: pH above 10.5 prevents hydrogen cyanide gas formation.

quiz.q: Which container material should NOT be used for cyanide leaching?
quiz.explanation: Galvanized metal contains zinc, which reacts with cyanide.

quiz.q: What is the typical dose of sodium cyanide per liter of water?
quiz.explanation: 0.5 to 2 grams per liter is effective and safer.

quiz.q: How long should leaching usually take?
quiz.explanation: 24 to 48 hours allows complete gold dissolution.

quiz.q: Which method is used to recover gold from pregnant solution?
quiz.explanation: Zinc dust causes gold to precipitate as a black mud.

quiz.q: What gas is formed if pH drops below 10?
quiz.explanation: Hydrogen cyanide gas is deadly and forms in acidic conditions.

quiz.q: What should you do if you smell bitter almonds during cyanidation?
quiz.explanation: Bitter almond smell indicates hydrogen cyanide gas; evacuate immediately.

quiz.q: Which protective equipment is essential for cyanidation?
quiz.explanation: A respirator with cyanide filters prevents inhalation of toxic gas.

quiz.q: Why should you never work alone with cyanide?
options: B) You may need help if poisoned
D) You need someone to talk to
quiz.explanation: A buddy can provide first aid and call for help if you collapse.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to dispose of cyanide waste?
quiz.explanation: Bleach neutralizes cyanide; test before disposal.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake in cyanidation?
quiz.explanation: Poor pH control leads to dangerous hydrogen cyanide gas.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel dizzy during cyanidation?
options: B) Get fresh air and seek help
quiz.explanation: Dizziness is a sign of cyanide poisoning; get fresh air immediately.

quiz.q: Which antidote is used for cyanide poisoning?
quiz.explanation: Amyl nitrite is part of the cyanide antidote kit.

quiz.q: How should cyanide be stored?
options: B) In a locked, dry, ventilated area
quiz.explanation: Cyanide must be stored away from acids and secured.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of adding lime in cyanidation?
options: B) To raise pH and prevent gas
D) To make it smell better
quiz.explanation: Lime raises pH, keeping cyanide in solution and preventing HCN gas.

quiz.q: What is the first step in cyanidation?
options: B) Crush ore to fine powder
quiz.explanation: Crushing increases surface area for cyanide to dissolve gold.

quiz.q: What is the pregnant solution?
options: B) The clear liquid containing dissolved gold
quiz.explanation: Pregnant solution is the gold-rich liquid after leaching.

quiz.q: Which method uses activated carbon to recover gold?
quiz.explanation: Activated carbon adsorbs gold from solution.

quiz.q: What should you do before disposing of tailings?
quiz.explanation: Neutralization prevents environmental contamination.

quiz.q: Why is ventilation important in cyanidation?
quiz.explanation: Good ventilation disperses toxic hydrogen cyanide gas.

quiz.q: What is a safe alternative to cyanidation for small-scale miners?
quiz.explanation: Gravity separation is safer and does not use toxic chemicals.

quiz.q: What is the recommended ratio of bleach to cyanide waste for neutralization?
quiz.explanation: One part bleach to ten parts waste neutralizes cyanide.

quiz.q: What should you do if you spill cyanide solution?
options: B) Evacuate and neutralize with bleach
quiz.explanation: Evacuate, ventilate, and neutralize with bleach to avoid gas.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of cyanide poisoning?
options: B) Headache and shortness of breath
quiz.explanation: Headache and breathing difficulty are early symptoms.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of the practical exercise?
options: B) To learn safe cyanidation under supervision
quiz.explanation: The exercise teaches the process with safety measures.

quiz.q: How can you test if gold remains in tailings?
quiz.explanation: Panning tailings shows if any gold was missed.

quiz.q: What should you do after finishing cyanidation work?
options: B) Wash hands and face thoroughly
quiz.explanation: Washing removes cyanide residues from skin.
